notes:
Maintainer risk: HIGH — 4 P0 correctness bugs: MTA-STS enforcer never wired in (delivery protection is a no-op), require_tls not persisted (RFC 8689 silently broken after queue persist), mta-sts.txt handler absent (Phase 1 unimplemented), REQUIRETLS not stored in SessionState (RFC 8689 silently broken in-session).
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: wfcj7.7 (domain validation — exploit requires attacker-controlled RCPT domain, which implies they already control delivery). wfcj7.9 (restart behavior — depends on deployment pattern). Uncertainty driven by: relay_queue.rs DrainOnce path not fully traced for all code paths. Would raise confidence if: confirmed that SmtpRelayQueue.start_drain and drain_once were fully read (only read to line ~200).
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — idiomatic in the critical paths; the string-wrapping errors and bool param are quality-of-life issues, not soundness problems. No unsafe issues found. The clone-on-cache-hit is a minor allocation overhead not currently visible in a hot path.
Rust idiom confidence: 10% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: wfcj7.19 (clone overhead — depends on mx_patterns size in practice). Uncertainty driven by: did not read relay_error.rs, routing.rs, queue.rs, or auth.rs in this pass — those are not in the MTA-STS scope.
title: Review: MTA-STS, REQUIRETLS, STARTTLS downgrade protection (stoa-2xeks)
